### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. **`@object-ui/react` `MetadataContextValue.readObjectScope` — accept set widened, docblock only.** RIGHT. The only change in `packages/react` is the docblock in `AppShellContext.tsx`: `{ names }` with no `packageId` is now a names-only scope; "neither" is the whole registry. The signature `(scope: { packageId?: string; names?: readonly string[] })` and the return shape (`objects`, `served`, `missing`, `settled`) are untouched; no member is added or retyped. The changeset's "No export, prop or type member is added" holds for `@object-ui/react`.
2. **Every existing caller passing `packageId` or nothing is unchanged.** RIGHT. In `MetadataProvider.readObjectScope` the new branch is `namesOnly = !scope.packageId && !!scope.names && scope.names.length > 0`; with a `packageId` the key is `scope.packageId` and every subsequent line (`whole.status === 'ready'` cut, `fetchScopeList`, the names loop) is byte-identical for that path. With `{}` or `{ names: [] }` `packageId` is `undefined` and the pre-existing whole-registry branch runs. The CONTROL pin in `MetadataProvider.namesOnlyScope-12980.test.tsx` pins both, and `AppContent.pageRouteObjects-12980` (b) pins the #12811 app-route call set. The refresh path skips `fetchScopeList` only for the `''` key. The `''` key cannot collide with a package id (ADR-0048 ids are non-empty).
3. **`@object-ui/app-shell` barrel — nothing new exported.** RIGHT. The diff touches no `index.ts`; `pageObjectNames`, `readPageObjectScope`, `PageRead` and the now-exported `navigationNames` are module exports of `console/appObjectScope.ts`, which the barrel re-exports by name only (it names `AppContent`, not that module), so they are internal. `GlobalSearchRenderer`, `NavMenuRenderer`, `InterfaceListPage`, `PageView` keep their prop types.
4. **`page/:pageName` in `APP_OBJECT_SCOPE_ROUTES` while the route table row keeps `['page','object']`.** RIGHT, and the dev's deviation is sound. #12811's own design puts `:objectName` in both tables: the scope list is what intercepts the `object` read for `AppContent`'s `allObjects`, and the `reads` row still serves the record overlay (`?recordId=` / `?form=`), which `hasRecordOverlay` excludes from the scope and which legitimately needs every object for related lists. The (a) pins run the real `AppContent` + `MetadataProvider` and assert no bare `object` call, which is the proof that the row's `'object'` entry does not fire on a scoped page open. Ablating the scope-list entry (dev's substitute ablation) is the equivalent of the order's literal one, since the row was never the mechanism.
5. **No whole-registry `meta/object` read on a page route in a package app.** RIGHT for the page, its view and the three blocks, pinned by (a) ×2 and (c). The route waits only on the page's own bound names (`ready = read(bound).settled`); the chrome's `requiresObject` names and the lookup targets of bound objects ride beside and are not waited for. Zero-binding pages (the measured pricing and welcome pages) read the package list the chrome reads anyway and nothing else, which is the card's Acceptance for item 1.
6. **What remains in a package-less app.** The chrome hooks `useNavMemberGates`, `useServedViewItems`, `useObjectPresence` still fall back to `objects` when the app has no `_packageId`, as #12811 left them. ACCEPTABLE for a `Part of` PR: those files were outside both the claim and the seat's widened surface; the measured control plane carries a package id so the card's Acceptance measurement is unaffected; the dev named the gap in the report's `out_of_scope_findings` and the PR's Acceptance notes. It must be carried as a follow-up on this card, not closed with it (see ③).
7. **`pageObjectNames` against the spec's page and block schemas.** MOSTLY RIGHT, with named misses. It collects the page's `object` (`PageSchema.object`, "Bound object (for Record pages)"), `interfaceConfig.source` (`InterfacePageConfigSchema.source`), every `objectName` at any depth (the `object-*` family's `objectName`, `record:related_list.objectName`, `record:reference_rail` entries, `action:*.objectName`), and `dataSource.object` (`ElementDataSourceSchema.object`, with the `api` arm correctly binding nothing). Strict schemas refuse the `objectName`/`from`/`source`/`entity` aliases, so the walker's spelling set is the published one. **Shapes a shipped block declares that it does NOT collect:** (i) `data: { provider: 'object', object }` — `ViewDataSchema`'s object arm on `object-grid` and `object-map` (`component.zod.ts` "Data source binding (ViewDataSchema — discriminated on `provider`: object | value | schema)"), the spelling `react-blocks.ts` calls the canonical one with the `objectName` alias retired; (ii) `element:metadata_viewer.object` ("Owning object — required for object-scoped kinds"); (iii) `record:line_items.childObject` / `parentObject`; (iv) `record:related_list.addPicker.object` and the PLANNED `parentDataSource.object`. Consequence: such an object is outside the page scope, so it is not in `allObjects` (chrome, command palette) and the navigator's `recordHref`/`listHref` answer null for it until the on-demand by-name read lands. It is never a whole-registry read, so the card's ruling holds; the block's own schema comes from the adapter, not the registry. This is a scope under-approximation with a working backstop, not a regression — flagged for a follow-up in ③, not a FAIL.
8. **On-demand read for an unlisted object (`PageView`).** RIGHT in mechanism: `requestObject` adds the name to a per-page-life `Set` (deliberately not state) and re-reads the scope, so the provider issues `GET meta/object/NAME` and the page re-renders when the scope entry settles; `recordHref`/`listHref` return null until then; `openRecord`/`openList` go through `whenKnown`, which navigates once `getItem` answers. Two things I could not verify from the diff alone and do not fail on: `whenKnown`'s `metadata.getItem` may issue a second by-name request beside the scope's own `fetchScopeName` if the provider does not share the item promise across the two paths (only reachable when a user clicks before the object lands); and `requestObject` is called from inside a child's render (the navigator is consumed by blocks while rendering), which is the same render-time read pattern #12811 and the `objects` getter already use. A hand-rolled context without `readObjectScope` falls back to `objects`, as the docblock says.
9. **`InterfaceListPage` reads `readObjectScope({ names: [cfg.source] })` with no `packageId`, even inside a package app.** PARTLY RIGHT. It removes the whole-registry read (pinned), but in a package app the route's `readPageObjectScope` already reads `interfaceConfig.source` under the package scope, and the names-only scope is a separate cache entry cut only from the whole registry, so the source object is likely fetched by name a second time. One small request, not 751 KB; escalated in ③, not a FAIL.
10. **`nav:menu` capability gate.** RIGHT. Reads `requiresObject` names under the app's package scope when it has one, names-only otherwise, `NO_CAPABILITY_SCOPE` when nothing is required; "registered unless the server answered without it" matches the sidebar's #12811 rule so the two menus agree. Note the gate's semantics on a hand-rolled context are unchanged (reads `objects`).
11. **`global:search` reads the registry only once the user types.** RIGHT. A search covers every object by definition; `ensureType('object')` in render is idempotent and fires only when `query.trim() !== ''`; `objects` is read only from then on. The census move to `action` (not `scope`) is the honest classification, and the test pins both halves.
12. **Census `openPathObjectReaders-12811`** rows for the four files move off `off` with reasons that match what the code now does. RIGHT.
13. **AGENTS.md #11 (no cross-file `path:line`)**: no new cross-file line address in the diff's comments, tests, changeset or PR body. Line Citation Gate is green.

No file outside the amended surface. ANSWERED.

3. Deviation 1 (ablation substitute: remove `'page/:pageName'` from `APP_OBJECT_SCOPE_ROUTES` instead of restoring the route row) — SOUND, see ① item 4; CONTROL stayed green, restore proven by blob hash.
4. Deviation 2 (`global-search-renderer` census row to `action`, not `scope`) — SOUND, see ① item 11.

The backstop (by-name on demand via the navigator) keeps the ruling intact; a follow-up should add `data.object` at least, since it is the spelling `react-blocks.ts` calls canonical for the object list.
